sentences.text: Tadzhikosuchus was an extinct neosuchian crocodyliform that lived in Tajikistan during the Late Cretaceous.
Scientists know this animal primarily from partial lower jaws, known technically as dentaries.
The type species, Tadzhikosuchus macrodentis, was described by Efimov in 1982 from fossils found in the Ialovachsk Formation of the Fergana Basin.
A second species, Tadzhikosuchus neutralis, was named by the same author in 1988 from that same location.
A third species, Tadzhikosuchus kizylkumensis, was described by Nesov and colleagues in 1989 from Turonian-age rocks in Uzbekistan.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Tadzhikosuchus within the parent group Crocodylinae.
This database also lists the family of Tadzhikosuchus as Crocodylidae.
Tadzhikosuchus lived between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Santonian stages.
A 2000 review by Storrs and Efimov suggested that the three named species could not be differentiated and should all be grouped under T. macrodentis.
Researchers could not determine the relationship between Tadzhikosuchus and Zhyrasuchus, or if they were synonyms, because the available fossils were poor.
